rationale: bugs_open/318. The release-coverage gate (register BLD-022) walks every production overlay and asks 'is the image this overlay pins one that the release builds?' — and CONTINUEs when the answer is no. That makes membership of RELEASE_IMAGES the gate's OWN admission criterion, so a service omitted from the list at birth is not uncovered, it is out of scope, and the gate prints 'Release coverage OK' about the exact omission it exists to catch. Eight services have fallen into that hole. Six were found and fixed by owner ruling on 2026-08-18; TWO MORE fell in afterwards — optional-explicit-wires-check (born 08-21) and commit-sha-exposure-check (born 08-22) — authored by sessions that had that ruling in front of them. The remedy currently in the makefile is a comment in capitals reading 'A NEW CHECK SERVICE MUST BE ADDED HERE IN THE COMMIT THAT CREATES IT', and CLAUDE.md's owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §2 already settles what that is worth: a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share. The cost when it bites is not uniform: several of these images compile the estate's action registry INTO the binary, so a frozen image is a frozen INVENTORY — measured 2026-08-18, removed-config-keys-check could see 165 of 169 registered actions and shared-output-fields-check 161, and a check that skips an action emits nothing, so its clean report is indistinguishable from a clean estate. This change INVERTS the predicate: an image of OURS that no release builds is now the violation, and the only way out is an explicit, greppable OWN_LINEAGE entry naming the target that does retag it. Two things follow from where the code lives. (1) SCOPE: scripts/council-scope.sh scopes review to platform/, internal/, pkg/ and appliable migrations, so a makefile-only gate cannot be reviewed at all — the existing one never was, and 318's own fix-candidate list warns 'decide the shape before assuming a review is available'. Putting the predicates in pkg/releaseset and leaving cmd/releasecheck thin is what makes this reviewable. (2) PROOF: on 2026-08-22 a session mutated the shared makefile IN PLACE to show the old gate discriminates and another session committed the file inside the window (WRONG_CALLS.md, f016b07ec); pure functions over parsed data make the mutation proofs table rows over testdata instead.
submitter: bugfix_318_release_source_coverage lane — the class fix for bugs_open/318, follow-on to bugs_closed/237 and register BLD-022

plan.summary: Move check-release-coverage's predicate from shell in the makefile into pkg/releaseset (reviewable, table-testable), and INVERT its admission test: an overlay pinning one of our images that no release builds is a violation rather than a skip. Adds the reverse-direction predicate BLD-022 §(iv) records as policed by nothing, and an opt-in OWN_LINEAGE exemption whose unsafe side is default OFF. The shell copy is DELETED in the same commit — two implementations of one gate is the drift class 099_SYNC_gate_roster.py exists for.

edits.rationale: Reads the four release declarations out of the makefile as LITERAL continuation blocks — deliberately not a make evaluator (the cron_parity_test.go idiom, one language over; decl_parity_test.go pays for the trade). The asymmetry in the required set is the load-bearing part: the three lists the gate uses to JUDGE are required, because an empty read of a list the gate uses to CLEAR a service is exactly how a check passes a tree it never measured. OWN_LINEAGE is optional because it is the clearing list and is legitimately near-empty, so absent and empty must mean the same thing or the first exemption anyone adds changes the meaning of every prior run.

The filesystem half. Two corrections to the shell gate's enumeration, both measured rather than speculative. (1) It walks overlays/production to ANY DEPTH: tools-api's real production overlay is at overlays/production/kustomization.yaml with no region directory, which the old fixed glob overlays/production/uk_001/... could never see. It pins a placeholder and has no workload, so nothing is broken today — but a real service at that depth would have been invisible for exactly the reason this bug exists. (2) It prefers newName over name, kustomize's own semantics: name selects what to rewrite, newName is what runs. Only one overlay uses newName today (that same placeholder), so this is a correctness fix for a LATENT case and is not claimed as a live defect. A missing services/ tree is an ERROR, not zero pins — zero findings over zero overlays is the shape of a check that never opened the tree it claims to have measured.

THE INVERSION IS THE FIX, and it is the one arm worth reading closely. The old gate: `case $RELEASE_IMAGES in *$img*) ;; *) continue;; esac` — non-membership was the ADMISSION test. Here, non-membership of an image of OURS is the violation (KindUnbuiltImage), and the only exit is an OWN_LINEAGE entry that names the target which retags it instead. The 237 direction is preserved unchanged as the second arm (KindNoReleasePath) and is pinned by test T3 so the port cannot silently drop what the predecessor already caught. InvalidDeployEntries adds the reverse direction BLD-022 §(iv) records as policed by NOTHING: a deploy entry whose resolved image is not in RELEASE_IMAGES would have deploy-agents retag that overlay to $(IMAGE_TAG) for an image nobody builds or pushes — the worked case being the two GitHub runners, which share one image and would ImagePullBackOff together, taking CI with them. Note this survived the build-backend derivation shipped earlier today (95757b6c2): deleting a name from RELEASE_IMAGES consistently stops it being built AND pushed, but the deploy loop still retags the orphan. Every Violation carries its remedy, which is the one habit worth keeping from the shell gate: a gate that says only 'no' gets worked around.

The instrument must be shown able to FAIL. Every case names in its comment what a different result would MEAN, because a green gate on a compliant tree proves nothing — it could only have passed, and BLD-022's own entry records that trap about its predecessor ('exercised, not proven'). T1 reproduces the exact 08-21/08-22 birth-omission shape; T2 is its negative control on the same tree; T3 reproduces the original bugs_closed/237 render-audit-adapter case so the port cannot drop it; T4 reproduces the paired-runner ImagePullBackOff; T5 exercises the exemption in BOTH directions (it must clear a reasoned entry, and must refuse a bare one and one naming a service with no overlay); T6 pins the depth correction; T7 pins that upstream images are never judged, because noise is fatal to a gate; T8 pins that an unreadable declaration is an ERROR and never a pass. Fixtures are temp directories, never the live makefile.

The price of a literal extractor instead of a make evaluator is drift — a declaration written in a form the extractor does not recognise reads as something else and the gate then polices a shape that does not exist. This is the payment: it asks MAKE for the same four lists (via new echo-only print- targets) and requires the readings to agree, in the style of cron_parity_test.go and optional_budget_cron_parity_test.go, which exist for exactly this reason one language over. It SKIPS LOUDLY when make is unavailable and never passes quietly — a silent pass here is the failure mode the test exists to prevent. setDiff reports a two-column difference rather than 'not equal', because the useful question when a parity test fails is always WHICH element moved. TestLiveTreeIsCompliant is a regression guard and is labelled in its own comment as NOT evidence the gate discriminates — the tree is compliant, so it could only have passed.

Thin CLI, the cmd/regcheck pattern: the operator runs the SAME code as the gate, never a re-implementation that can drift. Exit 0 clean / 1 violation / 2 COULD NOT RUN, and 2 is never conflated with 0 — a gate that passes what it failed to measure is this estate's own blind-pass landmine, shipped four days ago by the bugs_open/131 lane INSIDE the check written to end exactly that. The 1-vs-2 distinction is also printed in words because the makefile invokes this through `go run`, which collapses a non-zero child exit into its own 1 — MEASURED, not assumed: a throwaway os.Exit(2) program gives `go run .` 1 and its compiled binary 2. The makefile treats any non-zero as failure so the release stops correctly either way; what is lost without the words is an operator's ability to tell 'the release is wrong' from 'the check is broken'. The zero-our-pins guard is the same discipline one level up: reporting a clean release from an empty measurement is the failure this whole change exists to end.

edits.symbol: check-release-coverage, OWN_LINEAGE, print-release-images / print-agent-deploy-services / print-retag-exempt / print-own-lineage
edits.rationale: The rider, named rather than hidden: the shell predicate is DELETED and the recipe becomes `go run ./cmd/releasecheck --root . --registry $(REGISTRY)`. Deleting rather than keeping both is deliberate — two implementations of one gate is the drift class 099_SYNC_gate_roster.py exists for, and the Go side subsumes the shell predicate as test T3. Target name, call site (update-kustomization-images <- deploy-core <- release) and hard-gate status are unchanged: this is a continuation of the existing 237 gate, not a new seam. TWO THINGS THE COUNCIL SHOULD WEIGH. (1) The gate can now FAIL A RELEASE IT PREVIOUSLY PASSED — a birth-omitted service blocks where it used to be skipped. The consumer is the owner, who runs `make release` by hand, and he is told. (2) OWN_LINEAGE was going to ship EMPTY and the new predicate's FIRST LIVE RUN found a real entry for it: admin-dashboard pins docker.io/aqls/admin-dashboard, which build-backend does not build (it is a frontend, built from the working tree with no ref_build and no provenance stamp — BLD-019/BLD-020 scope frontends out explicitly), yet it IS released, as the last goal of pinned_sweep via release-dashboard. Genuinely own-lineage, genuinely covered, and NOTHING ON DISK SAID SO — the old gate could not have said so, because its image is not in RELEASE_IMAGES and that was the gate's admission test. The entry also records what it does not cover: release-backend omits release-dashboard, so a backend-only release leaves that service on its old tag.
edits.sketch:
.PHONY: check-release-coverage
check-release-coverage: ## Fail if an overlay pins one of our images but is in no release path
	@go run ./cmd/releasecheck --root . --registry $(REGISTRY)

# OWN_LINEAGE — the ONLY way an overlay may pin one of OUR images and stay out of
# the release. Entry form <service>:<the make target that retags it>. Opt-in with
# the UNSAFE SIDE DEFAULT OFF (CLAUDE.md owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2); it must stay
# a LIST, never a rule — a predicate that guesses which services are legitimately
# outside the release is one nobody can review.
OWN_LINEAGE := admin-dashboard:deploy-dashboard

.PHONY: print-release-images print-agent-deploy-services print-retag-exempt print-own-lineage
print-release-images: ## Print RELEASE_IMAGES (one line, space separated)
	@echo '$(RELEASE_IMAGES)'
print-agent-deploy-services:
	@echo '$(AGENT_DEPLOY_SERVICES)'
print-retag-exempt:
	@echo '$(RETAG_EXEMPT)'
print-own-lineage:
	@echo '$(OWN_LINEAGE)'

# DELETED in this commit: the 25-line shell predicate whose admission test was
# `case " $(foreach i,$(RELEASE_IMAGES),$(REGISTRY)/$(i)) " in *" $$img "*) ;; *) continue;; esac`
# — the `continue` that made membership of RELEASE_IMAGES the gate's own
# admission criterion, and printed "Release coverage OK" about eight omissions.

Mutation controls on a COPIED tree (never the live makefile): drop agent-chassis from AGENT_DEPLOY_SERVICES -> exit 1, 'NO RELEASE PATH: agent-chassis' (reproduces the original 237 state); drop content-loss-check from RELEASE_IMAGES -> exit 1, 'OUR IMAGE, NO RELEASE BUILDS IT: content-loss-check' (the birth-omission shape the old gate passed); empty OWN_LINEAGE -> exit 1 naming admin-dashboard; rename RELEASE_IMAGES away -> 'THE CHECK COULD NOT RUN', never a pass. Verbatim copy -> exit 0.
plan.risks: FOUR, named. (1) This replaces a LIVE, mutation-proven shell gate that the 2026-08-17 release already exercised. Mitigated by T3, which reproduces the predecessor's own discriminating control (the render-audit-adapter case), and by running both implementations over the live tree before the swap. (2) The gate can now FAIL A RELEASE IT PREVIOUSLY PASSED. That is the intent, but it is a behaviour change to a shared seam and the owner runs releases by hand, so he is told rather than merely measured at (CLAUDE.md owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3). Today's tree is compliant with one OWN_LINEAGE entry, so nothing blocks now. (3) A Go toolchain is now needed at deploy-core time. It is present on the release machine and its absence fails LOUDLY rather than silently — but `go run` collapses exit 2 into 1, so a scripted consumer cannot distinguish 'the release is wrong' from 'the check is broken'; the message says which in words, and a future non-makefile consumer should invoke the compiled binary instead. (4) ParseMakefileDecls is a literal extractor, not a make evaluator: a declaration rewritten as `+=` or `$(filter ...)` would read differently from what make sees. decl_parity_test.go pins the two readings against each other and reports a two-column diff, and it SKIPS LOUDLY rather than passing when make is unavailable. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, so the absences read as decisions: no git-history staleness detector (the pins' history is fiction here — deploy-agents seds newTag in place and nobody commits it; 26 overlays dirty and agent-chassis committed at v1.0.1239 against v1.0.1323 on disk); no gating of development overlays (only 9 services have one, and a hard failure would break every non-production deploy — BLD-022 §(i)); no cluster-side census in this round (it is detection, it needs RBAC, and it gets its own commit and its own review); no auto-remediation.
